title: When the Bakery Breaks
premise: Ansel Okafor, once the most sought-after wedding planner in Lagos and now a quietly burned-out one in London, has stopped believing in the ceremonies she sells. When her family reunion demands she arrive with a partner, she hires Theo Marsh, a widowed baker whose failing bakery sits beneath her office, to play her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date curdles into something real by dessert, forcing Ansel to confront why she fled love: her mother's dying wish that she inherit the family duty of keeping the Okafor name 'uncomplicated.' As Theo's bakery faces demolition and his visa clock runs out, Ansel must choose between the safe invisibility she built and a love that asks her to stay past the last train. She chooses him, publicly, at the reunion, and together they rebuild the bakery into something neither could have planned alone.
about_author: Astrid Okonkwo is a former event planner who traded seating charts for sentences after a decade of watching other people's happy endings. She writes warm, wry romances about people who are better at arranging love than admitting to it.

chapters.title: The Last Seating Chart
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She flawlessly executes a stranger's wedding while feeling nothing, then returns to her empty flat above the smell of Theo's midnight baking. Establishes her numbness and professional armor. Emotional beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: Bread Before Sunrise
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He bakes through grief for his late wife, fighting a demolition notice on the lease. Ansel descends for coffee; their first real conversation happens over proofing dough. Emotional beat: two insomniacs recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Reunion Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Her aunt Chiamaka calls: attend the family reunion with a partner or face the annual interrogation about her failed engagement. Ansel panics, then hears Theo arguing with his landlord through the floorboards. Emotional beat: desperation sparking an idea.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ansel offers him money toward the bakery debt if he plays her boyfriend for one weekend. He refuses twice, then accepts when the demolition date moves up. They draft rules: no real feelings, no questions about the past. Emotional beat: a contract built on avoidance.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They practice being a couple in the bakery—hand-holding, origin story, inside jokes—and it works too well. Ansel catches herself laughing genuinely and retreats behind logistics. Emotional beat: the first crack in the performance.

chapters.title: The Train North
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the journey to the family estate, they invent shared memories so smoothly that the invented ones start to feel like prophecy. A delay strands them talking for hours. Emotional beat: intimacy disguised as rehearsal.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Okafor compound swallows them: nosy cousins, her disapproving father, and Daniel—the ex-fiancé—unexpectedly present with his new wife. Theo's hand finds hers without prompting. Emotional beat: hostile territory, unexpected shelter.

chapters.title: Jollof and Interrogation
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the welcome dinner, Aunt Chiamaka tests him mercilessly; Theo answers with baker's honesty about grief, stunning the table. Ansel watches her family see her clearly for the first time. Emotional beat: truth as accidental strategy.

chapters.title: What Mama Left
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Her father privately reminds her of her mother's deathbed request: keep the Okafor name steady, marry sensibly, stop chasing other people's celebrations. Ansel realizes her career was always a rebellion. Emotional beat: inheritance as cage.

chapters.title: Kitchen Confessions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Escaping the party, they cook together in the old family kitchen. Ansel admits she stopped believing in weddings the day her own collapsed; Theo admits he said yes because he wanted the weekend to be real. Emotional beat: mutual confession, mutual retreat.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. During the reunion's talent night, they're pushed onstage together and improvise a dance that fools no one—including themselves. By dessert, the fake date feels devastatingly real, and both know it. Emotional beat: the point of no return, unspoken.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the dark veranda, an almost-kiss is interrupted by news: the bakery's demolition is confirmed for the end of the month, and Theo's visa renewal hinges on the business surviving. Emotional beat: joy ambushed by deadline.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The train back is quiet; each pretends the weekend meant nothing. Ansel drafts a cold text ending the arrangement, deletes it, sends a logistics email instead. Emotional beat: cowardice dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: Demolition Day Approaches
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Back in London, Ansel throws herself into a high-profile wedding while ignoring Theo's messages. She tours the venue and realizes she's planning someone else's forever to avoid her own. Emotional beat: avoidance reaching its limit.

chapters.title: Flour on His Hands
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo fights alone—petitioning the council, rallying neighbors—until Ansel appears unannounced with a legal contact and an apology made of action, not words. Emotional beat: showing up as the truest language.

chapters.title: Save the Date
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They work side by side to save the bakery, and the partnership turns tender. Ansel's client wedding collapses spectacularly due to her distraction, threatening her reputation. Emotional beat: the cost of divided hearts.

chapters.title: Her Father's House
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ansel's father arrives in London to deliver an ultimatum: abandon this distraction or lose the family's blessing and the seed money for her own company. Ansel must choose in front of them both. Emotional beat: duty versus desire, stated plainly.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Wounded and cornered, Ansel nearly boards the evening train back to her old life. At the platform she remembers her mother's actual last words—not duty, but 'don't shrink.' She lets the train leave without her. Emotional beat: the choice made in reverse.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Except Bread
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the council hearing, Ansel publicly stakes her name and savings on the bakery, exposing her family's expectations and her own fears in one speech. Theo, in turn, tells the room—and her—that he loves her. The building is saved. Emotional beat: love declared against all odds.

chapters.title: Crumb by Crumb
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rebuilding begins: repairs, a new sign, Ansel's resignation from the firm to launch her own planning studio above the bakery. Small domestic scenes show the relationship becoming ordinary, which is its own miracle. Emotional beat: love as daily practice.

chapters.title: The Reunion, Revisited
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. One year later, they return to the family reunion—this time honestly. Her father offers a grudging blessing; Aunt Chiamaka claims credit. Ansel introduces Theo not as a stand-in but as her home. Emotional beat: reconciliation and belonging.

chapters.title: When the Bakery Breaks Bread
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating POV. The bakery reopens with a new name honoring both their losses, and Theo proposes not with a ring but with a loaf scored with her initials. Ansel, the wedding planner who stopped believing, plans her own wedding down to the last detail. Emotional beat: second chances, perfectly timed after all.
